Compound: **nocodazole** (PubChem CID [4122](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/4122))

## Reflection

The correct Microtubule destabilizer call rested on sign, magnitude and monotonicity of tubulin loss rather than nuclear atypia alone: act_tub_ratio z=+43.4 at 3 uM and +20.1 at 0.1 uM with tub_mean strongly down, plus Spearman rho=-1.00 for tub_mean and +1.00 for act_tub_ratio across 0.01 to 3 uM, and a unanimous 10/10 destabilizer atlas match in e5. This matches the unblinded identity as nocodazole, described as a microtubule de-polymerising agent (PMID 16162358).

The real confound was Aurora kinase inhibition flagged by the microscopist in e4, which was plausible because both mechanisms produce failed mitosis, low solidity (z=-20 to -30) and large/multinucleated nuclei. I kept 7% on Aurora for that overlap but correctly down-weighted it because Aurora leaves polymer mass present while here tubulin was dim/diffuse with loss of filaments, and the atlas returned zero Aurora neighbours. - Used e2/e8 high-dose act_tub_ratio z=+43.4 to +20.1 and low nuc_solidity to anchor phenotype, then confirmed with e9 tub_mean rho=-1.00 and e10 act_tub_ratio rho=+1.00 monotonicity

- Rejected Actin disruptors despite act_mean z=+19.2 to +23.7 by recognizing increase was relative to tubulin loss, not actin depolymerization

What was wrong or missed:
- Left residual Aurora probability at 0.07-0.12 based on e4 visual multinucleation and e3/e8 nuc_solidity z=-24 to -30 without a direct Aurora-activity readout to close it
